recipes.name: Healthier Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients_raw: 2 (9 inch) unbaked whole wheat pie crust
1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cubed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Press 1 pastry crust into a 9-inch pie plate; refrigerate along with second pastry crust.

Combine chicken, carrots, green peas, and celery in a medium saucepan; cover with water. Boil until chicken is no longer pink in centers and vegetables are fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from heat, drain, and set aside.

Melt butter in a separate medium saucepan over medium heat. Add onion; cook until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in flour, salt, black pepper, and celery seeds; slowly stir in chicken broth and milk. Simmer over medium-low heat until thick, about 5 minutes. Stir in parsley. Remove from heat and set aside.
Transfer chicken mixture to crust in pie plate; pour broth mixture over top.
Cover pie with remaining pastry crust. Seal edges and cut away excess dough. Make several small slits on top to allow steam to escape.
Bake in the preheated oven until pie is golden brown and filling is bubbly, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool before serving for 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Chicken Pot Pie
raw_recipe.description: This healthier chicken pot pie recipe relies on a whole wheat crust, lean chicken, more vegetables, low-fat milk, and broth instead of canned soup.

review.reviewBody: I had half a roasted chicken leftover so I approached this recipe a little differently. I used 3 Tablespoons of grapeseed oil instead of the butter (a little healthier) and cooked the onion, diced carrots in the oil on medium low heat - I used 4 stalks of celery - add the celery to the onions and carrots and cooked for a couple of minutes. Add the flour, salt and pepper - stir to form a roux and then added about a cup of chicken broth, stir until it started to thicken and then added just a splash or two of milk - cook until thickened (adjust thickness after the sauce has come to a boil) I then stirred in the peas (I used more peas as I had a half a bag in the freezer) and the cubed, cooked chicken. Stir to combine. I want a thick mixture to fill the pie crust. You can add any vegetables you have on hand. If you have leftover cooked vegetables add them with the chicken. I used a basic short crust pastry recipe. The bottom crust will not be soggy if your chicken mixture is thick enough. If you want to cut out a few more calories use just a top crust.

It was a BIG hit with my family. I used a 10x15 lasagna pan. For the crust I just used 1 whole box of Krusteaz Pie Crust mix. I cooked my chicken in the crock pot for 7 hours in chicken stock. I added the veggies to this along with Parsley, Sage, Rosemary, and Thyme. I also added Baby Bella mushrooms, that I chopped, to the butter and onion mix. Followed the rest of the recipe to the letter.

I sautéed a diced chicken breast in 3 TBS of butter, along with 8 ounces of freshly sliced mushrooms and one diced celery stalk. I also added 1 tsp of minced garlic and about 1/4 cup of dried minced onions. After the chicken was no longer pink, I added a 12 ounce bag of frozen peas and carrots, low sodium chicken broth, milk and flour to the pan (I did not remove the chicken mixture). I omitted the salt and celery seed but used 1 tsp dried parsley. After simmering the mixture for 5 minutes, the "gravy" had thickened beautifully. I lightly oiled a 6 x 11 casserole dish and poured the chicken and veggies into the dish. I used one frozen pie crust and put it on top of the hot mixture. I baked it for 20 minutes and the crust was brown. We thought this was delicious and will be making it again. It's a little labor intensive but the taste is worth it. Servings = 4 for us.

We thought this was delicious! It made enough for at least two meals for the two of us. I forgot to add the parsley, and I used a combination of leftover roasted chicken and turkey, and I used a puff pastry sheet instead of a pie crust. I used low sodium chicken broth, but all I had on hand was whole milk. I put the filling in a 7x11 casserole dish and covered it with the puff pastry sheet. Yum! (Next time I will add some dried rosemary, thyme and sage, and I won't forget the parsley!)

This is s a good recipe to follow but I used a rotiserie chicken leftovers I had instead without boiling with the veggies. Also used some frozen peas and soup veggies along with the fresh carrots and celery. I always heavy up on my veggies and spice to equate. It has great consistency and flavor. Thanks for sharing.

I love this recipe, and its great for my son who has several food allergies. To simplify, I saute 2.5 -3 cups of veggies (carrots, onions, celery, peas) in 3 tbl butter. I saute 2 chicken breasts separately, and then add it to the veggies. When the veggies are tender, it mix in the flour, spices, and finally the chicken broth. Instead of cows milk I add a dash of almond milk. Cook on medium heat till thickens then pour into the pour into the pie crust and bake. Much easier
I've been making this recipe since 2008. I always add a potato and garlic.. Add "Better than Broth" chicken flavored to the water when I'm boiling the chicken and use that for my chicken broth later.

There really isn't much difference between this and the original, which I had been meaning to make. I normally use low fat or fat free milk anyway and the minimum amount of butter so that was in line with what's suggested here. However, it's much lower in fat and calories if you get rid of some of the pie crust. I had leftover chicken so boiled the veggies in the broth; reserved the broth; added 2T butter to the veggies, stirred in the flour, and then slowly incorporated the milk; returned the broth to the pot. When this thickened, I added the chicken and peas. I poured into two 4 x 7 baking dishes and used about 3/4 of a pie crust cut into rectangles to cover. (I saved the extra scraps for another use.) This was 4 hearty servings. By making those small changes, this calculated at about 416 calories and 17g fat at 4 servings or 208 cal and 8.5g fat for 8 (as written). Healthier is subjective, but I would prefer to have more substance and less wrapping for something like this.

This recipe is delicious, thank you so much for sharing! Even my husband who said he wasn't into chicken pot pie LOVED this and had seconds. Yesssss! Leftovers are (were) great. :-) The only thing I did differently based on input from others was cook the chicken mixture in chicken broth instead of water, and I added some poultry seasoning and about 2 teaspoons of the Chicken Better than Bouillon to the sauce mixture. Fabulous! I will be making several to freeze, also.

Cooked chicken and veggies in broth, then drained broth off to use. Subbed potatoes for peas. Added about an extra 1/2 cup liquid. Sauce was rather bland so I added extra pepper, Mrs. Dash, and Bavarian Inn Chicken Seasoning. Also couldn't find whole wheat crust so just used standard.

Tasted fantastic with these changes!

very tasty! added some garlic to the roux, and parmesan cheese before pouring the liquid mixture on top. followed others by simmering veggies in broth and reserving broth for the onions/roux. could use a little more seasoning next time, but nice overall, hubs and 6 yo dtr scarfed it up! hearty
This was very good. Made my own pie crust and added as well as chicken carrots, Brussel sprouts, red and green pepper and jalapeños. Worked out well.
Loved it. The grandma and mama approved, and it was healthy and tasty. It was a win all around!
I definitely will use chicken broth to cook vegetables in. It makes a robust taste. Only recipe I will use now!!!!
Tweaked a few things such as adding less of certain ingredients since I’m on a low sodium diet and it came out great. I used Marie C. Pie crust because it’s not made with LARD.
I followed the recipe and this turned out amazing!
first time making a pie and this came out pretty nicely (although i messed the middle up a bit)! it also tasted really good

I substituted unsweetened plain almond milk for the milk and decreased the broth to 1 cup, both of which worked well. I also used a whole wheat crust that included ground oats ,which was a terrific counterpoint in texture to the creamy interior. Using other veggies such as green beans and diced cooked sweet potato also works.

This recipe is so yummy. I am thrilled to make a healthier, homemade version. My husband loves peas, I don't, but I'll eat them in this recipe! The only problem I have is the overflow of ingredients when filling the crust, there is just too much of it. I can't seem to keep all it in the crust of a 9 inch deep-dish pie pan. I recommend using a little bit less of the filling. I also mixed the filling with the sauce before filling the crust which helped a little.
